You have Atlassian MCP tools available but DEFERRED. First run ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page" and max_results 2 to load the schema.

Then read these two Confluence pages IN FULL (convert_to_markdown=true, include_metadata=true):
1. Page ID 303104002 — "04.1.6 Regional Storefronts" (Req ID prefix REG)
2. Page ID 302710790 — "04.1.10 Analytics and AB Testing" (Req ID prefix AAB)

Context: I am researching the CONSENT position for a "Recently Viewed products" feature (stores a shopper's product browsing history — session-only for guests, account-persisted for logged-in shoppers) on the Zimmermann SFCC PWA storefront.

For EACH page report:
- The page's version number (from metadata) and any "last updated" / "extracted on" date stated in the body text.
- EVERY requirement row (quote the Req ID + the full requirement text verbatim) that relates to ANY of: consent, cookies, Didomi, GDPR/CCPA/privacy, tracking, personalisation, browsing history, recently viewed, data retention, or regional/per-storefront consent defaults. Include the Owner / Storefront / Config-Custom / Status / Comments column values for those rows.
- Explicitly state whether the page mentions "Recently Viewed" at all, whether it states any DATA RETENTION PERIOD for any personal/browsing data, and whether it distinguishes guest vs logged-in/authenticated treatment for any tracked data.
- Note any per-region differences (AU vs EU/UK vs US vs HK/ME) in consent defaults or opt-in behaviour.

Be exhaustive on the consent-relevant rows and quote them verbatim. Do not summarise away the exact requirement wording. Do NOT modify anything — read-only. Do not write any files. Return findings as your final message.

# Cross-page implications for a Recently Viewed feature

Six things that matter for the consent position, all sourced from the quotes above:

1. **Neither page contemplates the feature.** No requirement authorises, prohibits, or scopes browsing-history capture. Per AGENTS.md's Requirements rule this is a missing requirement, not an implied permission — it needs to be raised rather than assumed.

2. **AAB-003 is the closest governing principle and it cuts a specific way:** first-party data-layer population is explicitly *not* consent-gated ("regardless of consent state"); gating happens "at the tag layer" for "advertising and personalisation tags". A Recently Viewed list that is purely first-party (localStorage/session + SFCC account persistence, no third-party tag) sits on the ungated side of that line as written. But AAB-003 was written about the GTM data layer, not about storefront-owned persistent user data — reading it as authority for persisting browsing history is an extension of its scope, not an application of it.

3. **REG-051 has no consent category that fits.** The configurable set is Performance, Analytics, Marketing, plus non-configurable Required. There is no Functional/Preferences or Personalisation category — yet AAB-003 refers to gating "personalisation tags". So there is nothing in the confirmed Didomi taxonomy that a Recently Viewed store could be filed under other than "Required", which would be a substantive legal call, not a config decision.

4. **REG-049 vs REG-054 are in tension for AU/US-Intl/HK/ME.** REG-049 says scripts load only "after the customer has granted consent"; REG-054 says those four storefronts are "opted-in by default" with no action treated as consent. AGENTS.md's own "fail closed on consent" default sides with REG-049. Whichever way this resolves changes the default state a Recently Viewed feature inherits on four of eight storefronts.

5. **The account-persisted half falls squarely under REG-060/062/065.** If browsing history is written to the SFCC customer profile it becomes customer PII: it must be deletable on right-to-erasure (REG-060), exportable in a DSAR (REG-065), and auto-purged on the per-market retention period (REG-062) — and **no retention period is specified anywhere**, so that value has to be obtained before the persisted variant can ship. REG-066's consent audit log would also need to record consent for it if it is treated as consent-gated.

6. **UK has no confirmed consent default at all** (see the table above), and EU International is only covered by inference from "EU storefronts". Both are blockers for a per-region rollout decision.

**Data-quality note on the REG page, unrelated to consent but affecting trust in it:** REG-026 and REG-027 are near-duplicates that both route to HK — REG-027 reads "The system will route customers who select Australia from the country selector to the HK website", which contradicts REG-009's AU IP gating and REG-025's "AU storefront is gated and does not allow inbound cross-navigation". Also note REG-006 appears twice (two distinct requirements share the ID: EU domestic and EU international), and REG-001's requirement text says "7 independent storefronts" while its own Comments column says "Confirmed 8 storefronts" (REG-043 also says "11 active locales across 7 storefronts" while listing 8). Worth knowing the page carries these inconsistencies when citing it.
